# Security Research Legal Defense Fund

> The Security Research Legal Defense Fund (SRLDF) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, established in 2023, that provides financial assistance for the legal representation of good-faith security researchers who face legal issues due to good-faith security research and vulnerability disclosure, in cases that advance cybersecurity for the public interest.

The Fund promotes social welfare by helping good-faith security researchers defend against legal claims related to their research and vulnerability disclosure. The Fund may donate toward a researcher's own choice of counsel; it does not provide direct legal representation at this time. The Board of Directors considers potential grantees and votes on the distribution of funds.

## About
- [Home](https://srldf.org/): Overview of the Fund, its mission, and how it operates.
- [News](https://srldf.org/news/): Announcements and updates from the Fund.
- [Privacy policy](https://srldf.org/privacy-policy/): How the Fund handles personal information.

## For security researchers (grants & eligibility)
- [How it works / request a grant](https://srldf.org/#how-it-works): How to seek assistance and how grant decisions are made.

The Fund may donate to a good-faith security researcher's own choice of counsel to defend against claims related to good-faith security research or vulnerability disclosure. Anticipated eligibility criteria (subject to revision by the Board):
- Demonstrated financial need.
- Funds go toward representation in legal matters related to good-faith security research or vulnerability disclosure - not illegal behavior such as extortion.
- The activity was good-faith testing, investigation, correction, or disclosure of a security flaw, carried out to avoid harm to individuals or the public, with information intended primarily to promote security.
- Board approval.

## Board of Directors

- Kurt Opsahl (Filecoin Foundation)
- Harley Geiger
- Jen Ellis (NextJenSecurity)
- Casey Ellis (Tall Poppy Group and disclose.io)
